# flipper-flibuddy wire protocol, version 2

The Flipper app and the host (the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch apps)
exchange newline-delimited JSON over a byte stream: USB CDC (the Mac) or
Bluetooth LE (FliBuddy's own GATT service; the Flipper's Connection setting
picks one or, by default, runs both). The Flipper is a thin client: it sends raw tag dumps and user
actions, the host parses tags, talks to Bambuddy and sends back the spool's
fields, which the Flipper lays out itself, and display strings for errors.

Version 2 adds the Flipper's Auto-save new setting to every `scan`, the
structured `spool` / `tag_info` objects, and the actions `full`, `empty` and
`delete`. Version 1 hosts created every unknown Bambu tag on scan; a version 2
host does so only when the scan asks for it.

The contract is machine-checked:

- `schema/message.schema.json`: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for every message.
- `fixtures/messages/*.json`: at least one sample per message type, status
  and action, plus `scan_mfc_unreadable` (a MIFARE Classic whose sectors all
  failed), `scan_mfc_autosave` with the `lookup_created` that answers it, and
  `lookup_found_archived`. Files named `invalid_*` must fail the schema; every other file
  must pass.
- `fixtures/tags/*.json`: tag dumps, synthetic ones generated by
  `tools/fixtures/` and one real Phase 0 capture
  (`bambu_pla_pure_real.json`, `"synthetic": false`). `scan_*`,
  `intent_*` and `invalid_*` samples (except `invalid_missing_t`) are
  generated from the synthetic ones by
  `tools/fixtures/make_message_fixtures.py`.

The C (`flipper/tests`), Swift (`host/`) and Python (`tools/`) test suites
all run against these files. Changing a message means changing the schema,
the fixtures, this document and both sides in one commit.

## Framing

- One JSON object per line, UTF-8, terminated by `\n` (LF). A receiver
  accepts and strips a `\r` before the `\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
- A line, including its terminating `\n`, is at most **8192 bytes**. A
  receiver drops a longer line whole (everything up to the next `\n`) and
  keeps going. A sender never produces one; the Flipper reports an encoding
  error instead.
- Senders emit compact JSON (no whitespace between tokens) and no
  non-ASCII characters on the Flipper side. Receivers accept any valid JSON
  whitespace and any key order.
- Hex strings (UIDs, ATQA, blocks, pages) are upper-case without separators.

## Common fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `t` | string | Message type: `hello`, `scan`, `lookup`, `intent`, `result`. |
| `v` | integer | Protocol version, always `2`. |

A receiver reads `v` before anything else and ignores a line whose `v` is
not `2`, so a version 1 and a version 2 peer see each other as silent. The
host logs a peer speaking another version once ("Flipper speaks protocol 1,
host speaks 2") and shows it in its status. A receiver also ignores a line
whose `t` it does not know. A line that is not valid JSON, or a known `t` with missing or
ill-typed fields, is dropped as malformed; neither side crashes or
disconnects on it. Unknown fields are not allowed by the schema; a receiver
may ignore them.

## Session

1. After the transport connects, each side sends `hello` as its first line.
   On USB the Flipper sends its `hello` when the host opens the port (DTR
   raised).
2. The Flipper treats the link as **connected** once it receives a host
   `hello`. If none arrives within 2 s of its own, the port is probably held
   by something else (a terminal, qFlipper): the Flipper stays quiet, its
   status line shows `no host` and a scan stays local. A host `hello` that
   arrives later still connects. The Flipper answers a host `hello` with its
   own unless it is the reply to the Flipper's pending one. Closing the port
   loses the host. A Flipper on USB and Bluetooth at once (Connection =
   Auto) has one host: the first to say `hello` on either. It neither
   answers nor greets a host on the other transport while that host is
   connected, ignores what it sends, and greets it with a `hello` when the
   first host goes.
3. Flipper → host: `scan` after each tag read.
4. Host → Flipper: `lookup` answering that `scan_id`. With `autosave` on,
   an unknown tag that carries a material is created first and answered as
   `found` with `created: true`.
5. Flipper → host: zero or more `intent`s for that scan (user actions).
6. Host → Flipper: one `result` per intent, matched by `id`.

The host may also act on a scan by itself (the owner edits the weight in the
feed or presses New); that sends no `result`. When the owner creates the
spool on the host (New, or a Save on a tag no spool carried) or links the
tag to a spool there, the host sends a fresh `found` lookup, without
`created`, for the row's latest `scan_id`, whether or not the Flipper asked
for it (`link_on_host`, `create_on_host`). The Flipper replaces what it
shows with it while that scan is on its screen and ignores it otherwise. The
Python bridge has no host actions and sends none.

The host answers every valid `scan` with a `lookup`, `error` included. The
Flipper does not time out while it waits for a lookup ("Looking up"): Back
returns to Ready, and losing the host shows the scan's local facts.

## Messages

### `hello` (both directions)

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string, 1–40 | yes | Sender app and version: `flibuddy-fap/1.0` (Flipper), `flibuddy-ios/1.0.0` (iPhone and iPad host), `flibuddy-watch/1.0.0` (Apple Watch host), `flibuddy-mac/0.1.0` (Mac host), `flibuddy-bridge/0.1.0` (Python dev bridge). A host sends its bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString` (`dev` without one), cut to 40 characters. |
| `fw` | string, 1–40 | Flipper | Flipper firmware version, e.g. `1.5.1`. |
| `os` | string, 1–40 | host | Host OS, e.g. `macOS 26.0`. |

Exactly one of `fw` / `os` is present.

```json
{"t":"hello","v":2,"app":"flibuddy-fap/1.0","fw":"1.5.1"}
{"t":"hello","v":2,"app":"flibuddy-mac/0.1.0","os":"macOS 26.0"}
```

### `scan` (Flipper → host)

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scan_id` | id | yes | Unique per scan within a Flipper app run, `s-NNNNNN`. |
| `autosave` | boolean | yes | The Flipper's **Auto-save new** setting. `true`: the host creates an unknown tag that carries a material at once, with the tag's defaults. `false`: nothing reaches Bambuddy until the owner adds the spool (`new`, `weigh`, or the host's New / Save). |
| `tag` | tag object | yes | The raw dump, see below. |

Tag object:

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `"mfc"` \| `"ntag"` | yes | MIFARE Classic 1K or NTAG21x. |
| `uid` | hex, 4, 7 or 10 bytes | yes | Tag UID. |
| `sak` | integer 0–255 | yes | SAK from anticollision. |
| `atqa` | hex, 2 bytes | yes | ATQA as received, e.g. `0400`, `0044`. |
| `blocks` | object | `mfc` only, always present | Block number (`"0"`–`"63"`, decimal without leading zeros) → 16 bytes hex. Sector trailers (3, 7, …, 63) are never sent. Blocks of missing sectors are absent; `{}` when no sector was read. |
| `missing` | array of distinct integers 0–15 | `mfc` only, optional | Sectors that failed authentication or reading, ascending. Omitted when all sectors were read. |
| `pages` | object, non-empty | `ntag` only | Page number (`"0"`–`"230"`) → 4 bytes hex, from page 0 to the end of the tag's memory. |

The Flipper emits the `scan` fields, `blocks` / `pages` keys in ascending
numeric order and tag fields in the order of the tables; `scan_mfc.json` and `scan_ntag.json` show
the exact shape.

The Flipper reads a MIFARE Classic with Key A derived from a 4-byte UID (see
`flipper/src/bambu_keys.h`). A tag those keys do not open (any non-Bambu
MIFARE Classic, or one with a 7-byte UID) is still sent, with `blocks: {}`
and all 16 sectors in `missing` (`scan_mfc_unreadable.json`); the host
matches it by UID only and offers no prefill.

```json
{"t":"scan","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000012","autosave":false,"tag":{"type":"mfc","uid":"5A3C9E21","sak":8,"atqa":"0400","blocks":{"0":"5A3C9E21D9080400F600848E53F87010","1":"4130302D573100004746413030000000","2":"504C4100000000000000000000000000","…":"…"},"missing":[7]}}
{"t":"scan","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000013","autosave":false,"tag":{"type":"ntag","uid":"04112233445566","sak":0,"atqa":"0044","pages":{"0":"041122BF","1":"33445566","…":"…"}}}
```

A full Bambu dump (48 data blocks) is about 2 KB, a full NTAG216 dump
(231 pages) about 4 KB, both well under the line limit.

### `lookup` (host → Flipper)

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scan_id` | id | yes | The scan this answers. |
| `status` | `"found"` \| `"unknown"` \| `"error"` | yes | Spool found in Bambuddy, not found, or lookup failed. |
| `spool_id` | integer ≥ 1 | when `found` | Bambuddy spool id; equals `spool.id`. |
| `spool` | spool object | `found` only, optional | The spool, see below. A version 2 host always sends it with `found`; a Flipper without it falls back to `lines`. |
| `created` | boolean | `found` only, optional | `true`: the host created this spool from this scan (`autosave`). Absent means `false`. |
| `prefill` | boolean | `unknown` only, optional | The tag gave enough data (at least `material`) for the Flipper to offer **Add** (`new`) and **Add and weigh**. Absent means `false`. Equivalent to `tag_info.material` being present. |
| `tag_info` | tag info object | `unknown` only, optional | What the host parsed from the tag, see below. Absent for a tag without spool data (a blank NTAG, an unreadable MIFARE Classic). |
| `lines` | array of ≤ 4 strings, each ≤ 40 chars | yes | Display text, rendered verbatim: what the Flipper shows for `error`, and its fallback when `spool` / `tag_info` are absent. May be empty. |
| `defaults` | object | optional | Grams for the Enter weight screen: `gross` (last gross weight), `label` (filament weight per label), `core` (empty spool weight); each an integer 0–9999, each optional. |
| `error` | string, 1–200 | when `error` | Technical reason, for logs; `lines` carries what the user sees. |

Spool object (also in `result`):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer ≥ 1 | yes | Bambuddy spool id. |
| `material` | string, 1–40 | yes | E.g. `PLA`. |
| `subtype` | string, 1–40 | optional | As Bambuddy stores it, normally without the material (`Basic`); older spools may repeat it (`PLA Basic`). The Flipper titles the spool `material subtype`, or `subtype` alone when it already starts with the material (case-insensitive). |
| `color_name` | string, 1–40 | optional | Bambuddy's colour name, e.g. `Jade White`. Absent when unnamed; the Flipper then shows `Color #RRGGBB`. |
| `rgba` | hex, 4 bytes | optional | Colour as `RRGGBBAA`; the Flipper dithers its swatch from it. |
| `remaining` | integer 0–9999 | yes | Grams of filament left: `label` minus Bambuddy's `weight_used`, at least 0. |
| `label` | integer 0–9999 | yes | Filament weight per label (a full spool). |
| `core` | integer 0–9999 | yes | Empty spool weight. |
| `archived` | boolean | optional | `true`: the spool is in Bambuddy's archive (marked empty). Absent means `false`. |

Tag info object, each field present only when the tag carries it: `material`
and `subtype` (strings 1–40, `subtype` without the material as for new
items), `rgba` (hex, 4 bytes), `label` (integer 0–9999, label weight),
`color_name` (string 1–40, Bambuddy's name for the colour, resolved as for
new items, else Bambu's English name), `code` (string 1–16, Bambu's colour
code as printed on the box, e.g. `11803`), `filament_id` (string 1–16, the
filament id from block 1, e.g. `GFA01`), `diameter` (string such as `1.75`,
millimetres) and `nozzle_min` / `nozzle_max` (integers 0–999, °C). The tags
do not carry the colour code: the host finds it, and the English name, in
`tools/data/bambu_color_codes.json` (from Bambu Studio's
`filaments_color_codes.json`) by filament id and the colour part of the
variant id (`A01-N3` → `N3`), else by filament id and colour; new items get
it as `material_number`. The Flipper shows the colour name, then code,
diameter and label weight on one line; filament id and nozzle range are in
Tag details.

The host looks a tag up with `GET /inventory/spools/by-tag`, first by the
tray UUID and then by the UID. The tray UUID of a Bambu tag is block 9 as
32 upper-case hex characters: in Phase 0 it matched, byte for byte, the
`tray_uuid` an AMS had reported to Bambuddy for the same spool. A missing
or all-zero block 9 means no tray UUID, and the lookup goes by the UID
alone. Blocks 4+5 hold the detailed type and colour, not a tray UUID. Both
parsers (Swift `TagParser`, Python `bambu_tag`) read the tray UUID the same
way, and new items and tag links store it as `tray_uuid`.

The UID the host sends to Bambuddy (the `tag_uid` of the lookup, of new
items and of tag links) is the AMS form for Bambu tags: the upper-case UID
followed by `00000100`, so `7EF1AB04` becomes `7EF1AB0400000100`. An AMS
writes `ECA8FEDE00000100` for MIFARE UID `ECA8FEDE`, and Bambuddy keeps the
last 16 hex characters of whatever it receives without padding, so this
value round-trips unchanged and spools added by an AMS and by the Flipper
match. NTAG UIDs (7 bytes) are sent as read. The `lookup` lines and the
`scan`/`intent` messages carry the UID as read.

The host looks tags up with `include_archived=true`, so a spool marked
empty is still `found` (with `spool.archived: true`) when its tag is
scanned again, and never becomes a duplicate.

The Flipper pre-fills a gross weight with `spool.remaining + spool.core`,
falling back to `defaults.label + defaults.core`, and a net weight with
`spool.remaining`, falling back to `defaults.label`. `defaults.gross` is the
last gross weight Bambuddy recorded.

```json
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000012","status":"found","spool_id":42,"spool":{"id":42,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":484,"label":1000,"core":250},"lines":["PLA Basic","Jade White","484 g left of 1000","core 250 g"],"defaults":{"gross":734,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000012","status":"found","spool_id":42,"spool":{"id":42,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":0,"label":1000,"core":250,"archived":true},"lines":["PLA Basic","Jade White","archived","core 250 g"],"defaults":{"gross":250,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000015","status":"found","spool_id":31,"spool":{"id":31,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":1000,"label":1000,"core":250},"created":true,"lines":["PLA Basic","Jade White","1000 g left of 1000","core 250 g"],"defaults":{"gross":1250,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000012","status":"unknown","prefill":true,"tag_info":{"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","label":1000,"color_name":"Jade White","code":"10100","filament_id":"GFA00","diameter":"1.75","nozzle_min":190,"nozzle_max":230},"lines":["PLA Basic","#FFFFFFFF","label 1000 g"],"defaults":{"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000013","status":"unknown","lines":["NTAG","UID 04112233445566"],"defaults":{"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"lookup","v":2,"scan_id":"s-000012","status":"error","lines":["Bambuddy unreachable"],"error":"connection timed out"}
```

### `intent` (Flipper → host)

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | yes | Unique per intent, `i-NNNNNN`. The host's idempotency key. |
| `scan_id` | id | yes | The scan the action refers to. |
| `action` | enum | yes | See the actions below. |
| `grams` | integer 0–9999 | `weigh` | Weight typed on the Flipper. The Flipper sends it only with `weigh`. |
| `mode` | `"net"` \| `"gross"` | `weigh` | `gross`: spool on the scale as is. `net`: filament only; the host adds the spool's core weight (`gross = net + core_weight`) before `POST /spoolbuddy/scale/update-spool-weight`. The Flipper sends it only with `weigh`. |
| `tag` | tag object | yes | The same object as in the `scan`, so an intent is self-contained (a future offline queue replays intents without their scans). |

Actions:

| Action | Host does |
|---|---|
| `weigh` | Records the weight (`POST /spoolbuddy/scale/update-spool-weight`). On an archived spool it restores the spool first (`POST /inventory/spools/{id}/restore`). On a tag Bambuddy does not know ("Add and weigh" on the Flipper, autosave off) it creates the spool from the tag as for `new`, then records the weight. |
| `new` | Creates a full spool from the tag (**Add**; offered only when `lookup.prefill` is true). |
| `full` | **Mark as new**: restores an archived spool, then sets `weight_used` to 0 (`PATCH /inventory/spools/{id}`, with the spool's `weight_locked` as it was, since Bambuddy locks the weight when it is left out), so `remaining` = `label`. |
| `empty` | **Mark as empty**: sets `weight_used` to the label weight (`weight_locked` kept the same way), then archives the spool (`POST /inventory/spools/{id}/archive`). |
| `delete` | **Delete spool**: `DELETE /inventory/spools/{id}`. The tag is free to reuse. |
| `create_on_host` | Flags the feed row so the owner creates the spool on the host (a tag without material). |
| `link_on_host` | Flags the row so the owner links the tag to an existing spool on the host. |

`full`, `empty` and `delete` refer to the spool the tag is linked to; with
no such spool the result is `ok: false`. There is no undo on the wire: the
Flipper shows Mark as new / Mark as empty with a 3 s Undo before it sends
anything, and sends `full` / `empty` only when that toast commits (the bar
runs out, OK, Back, or a new tag). Delete is sent only from its
confirmation screen.

```json
{"t":"intent","v":2,"id":"i-000003","scan_id":"s-000012","action":"weigh","grams":734,"mode":"gross","tag":{"type":"mfc","uid":"5A3C9E21","…":"…"}}
{"t":"intent","v":2,"id":"i-000004","scan_id":"s-000012","action":"new","tag":{"…":"…"}}
{"t":"intent","v":2,"id":"i-000008","scan_id":"s-000012","action":"full","tag":{"…":"…"}}
```

### `result` (host → Flipper)

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | yes | The intent this answers. |
| `ok` | boolean | yes | Whether the action succeeded. |
| `lines` | array of ≤ 4 strings, each ≤ 40 chars | yes | Display text; the Flipper shows it on the Error screen. |
| `spool` | spool object | `ok: true` only, optional | The spool after the action (new remaining, the id of a spool just created). Absent after `delete`, `create_on_host` and `link_on_host`. |
| `error` | string, 1–200 | when `ok` is false | Technical reason, for logs. |

```json
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000003","ok":true,"lines":["Saved","484 g left"],"spool":{"id":42,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":484,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000004","ok":true,"lines":["Created","spool #31"],"spool":{"id":31,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":1000,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000008","ok":true,"lines":["Marked as new","1000 g left"],"spool":{"id":42,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":1000,"label":1000,"core":250}}
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000009","ok":true,"lines":["Marked as empty","archived"],"spool":{"id":42,"material":"PLA","subtype":"Basic","color_name":"Jade White","rgba":"FFFFFFFF","remaining":0,"label":1000,"core":250,"archived":true}}
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000010","ok":true,"lines":["Deleted","spool #42"]}
{"t":"result","v":2,"id":"i-000003","ok":false,"lines":["Not saved"],"error":"spool 42 not found"}
```

## Rules

- **Idempotency.** The host remembers every intent id it has completed in
  the session and answers a repeated id with the stored `result` without
  calling Bambuddy again; a repeat that arrives while the first is still
  running waits for the same result. Results of failed Bambuddy calls are
  not stored, so a repeat retries them. A `weigh` on an unknown tag looks
  the tag up again before it creates the spool, so a repeat after the
  create succeeded and the weight failed weighs that spool and never
  creates a second one. The Mac host keeps the last 256
  results. A repeat is the same intent again: a known id with any other
  field changed (a restarted Flipper may reuse an id) is performed as a new
  intent, after one still running under that id, and replaces the stored
  result.
- **Matching.** The Flipper applies a `lookup` only if its `scan_id` is the
  scan on screen (a later one for the same scan replaces the earlier), and a
  `result` only if its `id` is the intent in flight; anything else is
  ignored.
- **Timeouts.** The Flipper waits 10 s for a `result`, then shows an error.
  The host does not time out on the Flipper.
- **Send failures.** A side that cannot send does not leave the other
  waiting: a Flipper whose `scan` does not go out whole shows the tag's
  local facts, one whose `intent` surely did not go out shows an error at
  once, and one whose `intent` may have arrived (only its end was not
  taken) waits for the `result` or the timeout; a host that cannot send a
  `lookup` or `result` closes the port (the Flipper sees the host go) and
  reconnects. A Flipper line cut short is ended by an empty line sent
  before the next one, so the receiver drops the fragment as malformed
  instead of joining it to the next line.
- **Wording.** The host owns the text in `lines`; the Flipper lays out
  `spool` / `tag_info` with its own labels. It renders `lines` verbatim and
  never parses them. Its screen is ASCII-only: each
  control character or non-ASCII character in a string shows as `?`, so
  the host keeps `lines` ASCII where it can.
- **New items.** The Flipper never sends `new`, or `weigh` for an unknown
  tag, without `prefill: true`, and the host refuses to create a spool
  without `material`. The host names the
  colour from Bambuddy's colour map (`GET /inventory/colors/map`, loaded once
  after the start-up check): `by_material["<detailed type>|<hex6>"]`, then
  `colors["<hex6>"]`, lower-case, alpha dropped. Without a match, or when
  the map failed to load, `color_name` is left out, never a hex string.
  `subtype` is the detailed type without a leading word equal to the
  material, case-insensitive ("PLA Basic" → "Basic", "PETG-HF" stays), as
  on spools an AMS adds; nothing left means no `subtype`. The Flipper's
  `lookup` lines and the host feed still show the full detailed type.
- **Create on scan.** The host creates a spool from a scan only when the
  scan has `autosave: true` and the tag carries a material; otherwise an
  unknown tag stays unknown until an intent (`new`, `weigh`) or the owner
  on the host adds it. A rescan of a tag created on scan finds that spool
  and creates nothing.
- **Inventory mode.** The host checks `GET /settings/spoolman` and refuses
  to work against a Bambuddy in Spoolman mode: the Mac host answers every
  `scan` with an `error` lookup and every intent with `ok: false`, both
  saying why; the Python bridge exits at start-up.

## Identifiers

`scan_id` and `id` are strings of 1–32 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 _ . : -`.
The Flipper uses `s-` / `i-` followed by a zero-padded counter.
